newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Hardline former Yeltsin aide Yegorov dead at 45.
newsitem.headline: Hardline former Yeltsin aide Yegorov dead at 45.

text.p: Nikolai Yegorov, former chief-of-staff to President Boris Yeltsin and seen as a leading proponent of the hard line that led to war in Chechnya, died on Friday at the age of 45.

A Kremlin spokesman said on Sunday that Yegorov, who was the minister for ethnic minorities when Yeltsin ordered troops to crush the secessionist Chechen leadership in December 1994, had suffered from a long illnesss.

One of a number of senior officials removed after Chechen guerrillas staged a bloody hostage-taking raid on the Russian town of Budennovsk in June 1995, Yegorov made a comeback as Yeltsin's chief-of-staff in January 1996.
He was sacked in July last year in a cull of Kremlin hawks following Yeltsin's re-election, making way for the liberal Anatoly Chubais, who is now first deputy prime minister.
After returning last summer to his earlier post as governor of the southern Krasnodar region, close to Chechnya, Yegorov lost his job to a communist opponent in an election in December.
